heroHeadline: Day 369: India Hosts BRICS FM Summit as Ceasefire Holds — Pakistan IBO Claims 'Indian-Backed' Militants in Balochistan
heroSubtitle: May 14, 2026: India's EAM S. Jaishankar chaired the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Summit in New Delhi (May 13–15), with Iran-UAE tensions dominating the agenda — no India-Pakistan bilateral contact occurred on the sidelines, reaffirming India's condition that talks await Pakistan's dismantlement of cross-border terrorist infrastructure. On May 13, Pakistan Army's ISPR announced an IBO in Barkhan, Balochistan, killing 7 militants it labeled 'Indian-backed Fitna al-Hindustan' — 5 Pakistani soldiers including a Major were martyred. The ceasefire along the Line of Control, now at 369 days, continues to hold with no major kinetic incidents on May 13–14. The bilateral freeze remains total: mutual airspace closure in force through May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, no ambassadors exchanged, all trade halted.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
